title: I use these 5 Gemini prompts to make Google Maps even more powerful
excerpt: Get more out of Google Maps with Gemini
content_html:
Published Nov 25, 2026, 8:02 AM EST

Sanuj Bhatia is a consumer technology journalist who has been writing about smartphones, wearables, tablets, and consumer electronics since 2018. At Android Police, he covers everything from the latest Android smartphones and software updates to Google apps and services, with a particular focus on hands-on testing. 

Before joining Android Police, Sanuj served as News Editor and later as Managing Editor at Pocketnow (2023–2024). His work has also appeared in Tom's Guide, Android Central, Android Authority, Pocket-lint, MakeUseOf, TechRadar, and SoundGuys.

In addition to covering devices, Sanuj has also attended major international technology events, including MWC (2024, 2025, and 2026), IFA (2024, 2025, and 2026), and Computex 2026.

He holds a bachelor's degree in engineering (Computer Science) and an MBA. When he's not writing about technology, you'll often find him experimenting with custom Android ROMs, working on Raspberry Pi projects, enjoying a cup of chai, or watching Chelsea play.

You can reach him at sanujb6 [at] gmail [dot] com.

Google has been adding Gemini to almost every part of its ecosystem, including Android. We recently saw how the Create My Widget feature works, allowing Google Pixel users to create customized home screen widgets using Gemini.

But beyond Android, Google has also been expanding Gemini's capabilities across its other apps. Earlier this year, Google brought Gemini to Google Maps with a new feature called Ask Maps.

Google Maps has always been my go-to navigation app. But lately, I've started using it a little differently. Instead of searching for individual places, scrolling through reviews, and jumping between different locations, I've been using Gemini directly inside Google Maps to find exactly what I'm looking for.

And after trying it on my recent trips, I've found five prompts that have made exploring unfamiliar cities a lot easier.

Ask Maps is more useful than you might think

Gemini lets you ask more specific questions without digging through Google Maps results

If you haven't heard about it yet, Google has integrated Gemini directly into the Google Maps app. You'll find a small chip labeled Ask Maps just below the main search bar, where you can access the feature.

What Ask Maps essentially does is let you ask complex, conversational questions directly inside Google Maps instead of relying on traditional searches.

For example, instead of simply searching for "restaurants near me," you can ask Maps to find a quiet restaurant serving vegetarian food within walking distance of your hotel.

You can even ask more specific questions like, "Which spots from my saved lists have availability for two people for dinner tonight and also allow pets?"

I've started making the most of it whenever I'm traveling, especially when visiting a new country, and it's proven to be incredibly helpful. It might seem like a small addition to Maps, but after you start asking more specific questions, you realize just how useful it can be.

These 5 Ask Maps prompts made my trips easier

From finding vegetarian food to watching Chelsea, these are the prompts I keep using

I made the most of Ask Maps during my recent trip to Portugal, and I found myself relying on it more than I expected. Since then, I've also used it during my trip to Thailand, and here are five prompts that I keep coming back to:

1. Finding vegetarian food without the hassle

One of the biggest challenges I face when traveling internationally is finding good vegetarian food. I'm vegetarian (although I do eat eggs), and options abroad can sometimes be limited unless I stick to things like salads.

Now, instead of searching for vegetarian restaurants, applying filters, and going through menus individually, I simply ask Maps, "Find me authentic local restaurants nearby that serve good vegetarian food, including dishes with eggs."

This helps me find places that fit my preferences while still getting to experience the local cuisine.

2. Finding a quiet cafe to get some work done

Because I mostly travel for work, there are times when I need to sit down and finish an article or catch up on emails. But finding a cafe with good Wi-Fi and, most importantly, a quiet atmosphere isn't always easy.

That's where Ask Maps comes in. I simply ask, "Find me a quiet cafe nearby with Wi-Fi, charging outlets, and enough space to work on my laptop for a couple of hours."

Instead of making me go through dozens of cafe reviews to figure out which ones are suitable for working, Ask Maps helps me narrow down the options in one go.

3. Finding somewhere to watch Chelsea play

I'm a huge Chelsea fan, and whenever I'm traveling during a match, I try to find somewhere I can watch the game. The problem is that finding a good sports bar overseas isn't always easy. Now, I can simply ask Maps, "Where can I watch the Chelsea match tonight near my hotel?"

It's a much easier way to find potential places showing the game without manually searching for sports bars and checking each one individually.

4. Making the most of a few free hours

When I'm traveling for work, my schedule is usually packed with meetings and events. But every now and then, I get a few hours to myself, and I don't want to spend most of that time figuring out where to go.

So I ask Maps, "I have three hours free before my next meeting. What can I explore nearby without traveling too far?"

What I like about this prompt is that it takes my limited time into account rather than simply suggesting the most popular tourist attractions.

5. Exploring a city after dark without going clubbing

One thing I really enjoy when visiting a new country is walking around the city in the evening. That said, I'm not really a fan of bars or clubs. Most of the time, I just want to find a nice neighborhood to walk around, grab something to eat, or spend some time outside.

So I ask Maps something like, "I want to explore the city after dinner, but I'm not interested in clubs. Where can I go for a nice walk or enjoy the nightlife?"

It's helped me look beyond the usual nightlife recommendations and find places that better align with how I actually like to explore a city.

It's not perfect, but it's a great addition to Maps

Of course, Ask Maps isn't perfect. There have been times when the suggestions weren't exactly what I was looking for, and I'd still recommend double-checking important details like opening hours or whether a place actually offers what you need.

That said, I've found Ask Maps to be a genuinely useful addition to Google Maps, especially when I'm traveling somewhere unfamiliar. And beyond Ask Maps, there are plenty of other Google Maps features worth trying that can make traveling and getting around much easier.
